summary.intent: Implement the full shared-folder move feature across all layers (todos #7 and #8): let a write-permission share recipient move a file between subfolders within a single share with correct FileMetadata re-encryption, and consolidate the duplicated ECIES key-unwrap in useFolderNavigation into the SDK.
summary.outcome: Session produced a comprehensive 5-agent codebase investigation mapping all relevant layers, locked scope decisions with the user, and scaffolded Phase 49 in ROADMAP.md and STATE.md with full requirements. No implementation code was written; the phase is ready for /gsd-plan-phase 49.

repo: sharedFolderTree holds only ONE folder depth at a time (re-seeded on navigation); a cross-subfolder move must resolve destination subfolder keys on-demand from share_keys (keyType 'folder'/'folder-ipns') rather than reading cached state.

reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange (packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts) is fully key-agnostic — takes explicit sourceFolderKey/destFolderKey — and is reusable verbatim for the shared-move case with no changes.

Phase 48 (PR #505) already shipped: sharedFolderTree keyed by shareId, client shared methods, adoptSharedFolderResult, sharedFolder:updated event. The shared-move phase builds directly on top of this; no new infrastructure needed.

FileMetadata IPNS records are AES-256-GCM sealed under the PARENT folder's folderKey. Any parent change requires re-sealing under the destination folderKey via updateFileMetadata({createVersion:false}) or every subsequent decrypt throws DECRYPTION_FAILED.
File share_keys entries are keyed by itemId, not folder position, so a move does NOT require issuing fresh recipient share_keys entries for the moved file.
The private web MoveDialog reads the private useFolderStore tree and cannot be reused for the shared context — a new SharedMoveDialog rendering the lazily-enumerated shared subtree is required.
ContextMenu already has an optional onMove prop in the codebase; it just needs to be wired in SharedFileBrowser's folder-view ContextMenu.

ensureFolderLoaded/loadFolderMetadata returns null immediately with no retry logic; the web side must add its own 3×/2s IPNS-propagation retry wrapper to avoid breaking navigation into just-created folders.
ROADMAP and STATE were out of sync after Phase 48: all 7 plans shown as shipped in STATE but Phase 48 REQ-2 checkbox was still unchecked in ROADMAP.md.

The reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange function is idempotent: if decryption under sourceFolderKey fails with DECRYPTION_FAILED, it attempts decryption under destFolderKey; success means a prior partial attempt already re-keyed, so it returns early rather than erroring.

code.finding: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange — key-agnostic helper reusable verbatim for shared-folder move; includes idempotency guard via DECRYPTION_FAILED retry under destFolderKey

moveItem (private vault) — canonical 8-step sequence to mirror: requireFolder both sides → snapshot base children → pure sdkCore.moveItem → publish DEST first → re-key FileMetadata → publish SOURCE → adopt publishedChildren (not locally-computed) → emit folder:updated
updateSharedFile — existing shared analog showing the addShareKeysFn + owner/recipient key wrapping pattern that moveInSharedFolder must follow
moveItem — pure function (no I/O); throws 'An item with this name already exists in destination' on name collision; must be called before any publishes
updateFolderMetadataAndPublish — wraps publishWithCas with CAS/409-merge/retry (up to 4 attempts); must adopt publishedChildren from result, not locally-computed children

Hand-rolled ECIES unwrap + IPNS-resolve + decrypt to be replaced by client.ensureFolderLoaded(); must preserve 3×/2s retry and clone SDK-owned key buffers into FolderNode to avoid use-after-zero on client.destroy()
restoreFromBin — second reference for the re-encrypt pattern; confirms the re-key step happens AFTER destination publish (add-before-remove crash safety)
